notes: Three rules in testing.md changed in the working tree since 93873be and were graded against the current text: "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour", "Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`" and "Run tests concurrently unless they share global state". The other four graded rules are unchanged and were graded to the standard of the 2026-10-21 grade files.

Grouping is now decided by testing.md: "Name a `describe` block after the function under test, or after a condition its tests share, the shape the ExUnit documentation shows with a named `setup` (`describe "when the subscriber has exited" do` followed by `setup [:subscribe_and_exit]`)." Counts: a block joining two functions in 0 of 4 runs; a test name stating only its return value in 0 of 4 runs; a scenario describe, now allowed, in 4 of 4 runs (haiku-1 line 95; haiku-2 lines 129 and 164; sonnet-1 line 123; sonnet-2 lines 136 and 167). Under the 93873be text these scenario describes would have been violations, as they were in all five skill runs of the previous sweep.

start_supervised is now decided by testing.md: "To assert that a start fails, call `start_supervised/1` and match the reason." and "a server that registers `__MODULE__` by default takes the test's own name from the context, `name: context.test`." Counts: start_link called from a test in 1 of 4 runs (sonnet-1 line 41); a server under the default global name in 0 of 4 runs. sonnet-2 asserts the start failure with start_supervised/1 and a matched reason (line 48); haiku-1 and haiku-2 have no start-failure test. Previous sweep: 2 of 5 skill runs violated.

Concurrency is now decided by testing.md: "`Process.register(self(), TestMailer)` and `Application.put_env(:notify, :test_pid, self())` make the test process a singleton, which forces `async: false`." Count: async: false because of the test's own singleton in 0 of 4 runs; all four use async: true and register the test process in a Registry under the server's test name, the shape the new paragraph shows. Previous sweep: 3 of 5 skill runs violated.

Unchanged rule "Assert with patterns": sonnet-2 lines 55-56 (assert [pid] = ..., then assert pid == self()) are graded violated because they follow the rule's first "Instead of" example, a match followed by == on the bound part; the case's check names assert [^pid] = ... as the expected form. It is the only violation of that rule in this batch.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs, three times each with random seeds; results were the same each time and there were no compiler warnings. sonnet-1 fails mix format --check-formatted only because of an extra blank line at the end of the file.
